title: North and south Indian temples tell you apart by the tower
sources: NCERT Class 11, An Introduction to Indian Art, ch. 6 'Temple Architecture and Sculpture'

quiz.why: Right. Gopurams are the gateway towers of Dravida temple compounds.

review.note: Written and voiced by Claude (AI voices, Kokoro), 8 Nov 2026. Not yet checked by a subject or Hindi editor. Vesara (mixed) style left out for length.

lines.say: Look at the tower, and you can tell where a temple comes from.
Curved in the north. Stepped like a pyramid in the south.

data.headline: Nagara and Dravida: two temple styles

beats.say: Look at the tower, and you can tell where a temple comes from. Curved in the north. Stepped like a pyramid in the south.

lines.say: Nagara temples have a curving tower called the shikhara.
They usually sit on a raised platform, often without big boundary walls.

items.sub: A curving tower over the sanctum

beats.say: Nagara temples have a curving tower called the shikhara. They usually sit on a raised platform, often without big boundary walls.

lines.say: Dravida temples have a stepped tower called the vimana.
And a walled compound entered through tall gateways called gopurams.

items.sub: Tall gateways in a walled compound

beats.say: Dravida temples have a stepped tower called the vimana. And a walled compound entered through tall gateways called gopurams.

lines.say: The Kandariya Mahadeva temple at Khajuraho is Nagara.
The Brihadeeswarar temple at Thanjavur, built under Rajaraja Chola, is Dravida.

data.text: Kandariya Mahadeva, Khajuraho: Nagara. Brihadeeswarar, Thanjavur: Dravida.
